page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.32xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 128 vCPUs and 64 physical cores utilizing the x86_64 architecture with Intel Xeon 8375C processors running at 3.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4096.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 32.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is bundled as a 3800 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance supports a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing and memory capabilities. The Passmark CPU score is in the top tier at 85,629.49, and the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is strong at 123,925.38. Memory bandwidth is also strong, reaching 302.32 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 122.18 GB/sec for large block write operations. In database-specific testing, the instance achieved 106.84 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and scored 29,714.26 in Passmark database operations.

This instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale databases, and enterprise applications. While it demonstrates strong performance in multi-threaded tasks and database operations, its single-core performance is average, as shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1893.7. Additionally, without dedicated GPU hardware, it is less suited for large-scale LLM text generation, where it achieves a weak 2.76 tokens/sec on a 70B model. The high resource density of 4 TB of RAM and 128 vCPUs makes it a highly specialized, cost-efficient option for consolidating massive in-memory databases and enterprise workloads that require high network throughput and local NVMe storage.
